Dick Cheney was the forty-sixth Vice President of the United States, serving under George W. Bush from two thousand one to two thousand nine, and is regarded as one of the most powerful and controversial vice presidents in American history. Before his vice presidency, he served as Secretary of Defense under President George H. W. Bush, supervising Operation Desert Storm during the first Gulf War. Cheney also previously served in the House of Representatives from Wyoming as a powerful minority whip, leading House Republican operations. As Vice President, Cheney wielded unprecedented influence over foreign and defense policy, effectively serving as co-president in Bush's first term after the nine-eleven attacks. He advocated strongly for the two thousand three invasion of Iraq, claiming Iraq possessed weapons of mass destruction that investigations later failed to confirm. Cheney championed an expansive interpretation of executive power and authorized controversial interrogation practices including waterboarding. In two thousand six, he shot hunting companion Harry Whittington in a quail-hunting accident, an incident that became a cultural touchstone for media satire. He left office with low approval ratings due to his association with unpopular wars and remained a controversial figure in conservative politics afterward.
